title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming formatting
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to feature parity with respect to request parameters (temperature, top_p, n, presence/ frequency penalty), role handling for system/user/assistant messages, stop sequences and logprobs passthrough, and response formatting for streaming clients. This PR centralizes compatibility logic, fixes several streaming stability edge-cases, and tightens tests and documentation. Changes in this PR: - Support for explicit params mapping (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, n, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty) and validation against Redwood runtime limits. - Accurate preservation and round-tripping of roles (system, user, assistant) into internal message structures and back for responses and deltas used in streaming. - Stop sequence handling compatible with OpenAI semantics (multi-token stops, precedence between stop and max_tokens, early termination semantics) and related unit tests. - logprobs passthrough for deterministic model backends: when client requests logprobs, we attach model-provided token logprobs in the compatibility response envelope. - Streaming response formatting: ensure chunked events align with OpenAI delta shapes; fix race where final 'done' event could be emitted before trailing metadata (finish_reason, index) was attached. - Improved retry and backpressure handling in streaming transport to avoid duplicated tokens under transient reconnects. - SDK/Examples: updated Python and TS quickstarts and a new streaming example demonstrating role echoes, stop-sequences, and logprob inspection. - Docs: expanded API compatibility notes and caveats for degenerate stop/logprob combinations. Checklist: - [x] Core parameter mapping and validation - [x] Role preservation tests - [x] Stop handling + unit tests - [x] Streaming stability fix + integration tests - [x] SDK examples updated - [x] Docs and release notes drafted Testing & verification: extensive unit tests added (runtime, compatibility layer, streaming harness). Integration tests run against small LLM runtimes and internal mock OpenAI gateway. CI flaky test 'streaming_integration_test::reconnect_sends_no_duplicate_tokens' was rerun once and stabilized after adding a short debounce in the transport layer. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged when clients call Redwood-native endpoints; compatibility layer gated behind /openai prefix and feature flag. Migration: no customer migration required. Notes: There are a couple of followups tracked in ENG-4020 (streaming metrics for per-chunk latency) and ENG-4018 (support for structured function call responses in streaming mode, edge-case around arrays in stop tokens).
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial params mapping and validation; role serialization fixes; stop-sequence engine and tests; streaming transport debounce + fixes; SDK examples and docs; test flakiness fixes and CI config updates.
review_thread: Initial review requested changes on role round-tripping and stop precedence (Ethan). Author addressed by normalizing role enums and adding an explicit test matrix. Carlos called out potential perf regression for param validation on hot paths; author moved validation to request-parsing stage and added microbenchmarks. Lena requested clearer doc examples and a streaming example showing stop sequences; added. CI: streaming_integration_test flaked once; fixed by adding 50ms debounce in transport reconnect logic and protecting finalization path with a single-flight guard. After fixes, reviewers approved and requested squash merge.
ci_checks: integration: pass (streaming harness against small runtime)
release_notes: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: added support for common OpenAI parameters (temperature, top_p, n, penalties), improved role handling, OpenAI-compatible stop sequence semantics, logprobs passthrough where available, and more stable streaming formatting. See docs/openai_compat.md for details and caveats.
notes: Followups tracked: ENG-4020 (streaming chunk metrics), ENG-4018 (structured function call streaming edge-cases).
